home.title: See if the CalFresh work rule applies to you
home.subtitle: Answer a few short questions. It takes about 2 minutes.
home.cta: Check if the rule applies to you

checklist.title: Do any of these apply to you?

result.notDecision: This is not a decision. Only your county can decide.
result.sayIntro: When you call, you can say:

not_subject.title: The rule likely doesn't apply to you.
not_subject.body: You don't need to report work hours for this rule right now.

possibly_exempt.title: You may be exempt. Ask your county to confirm.
possibly_exempt.body: Tell your county about your situation. They will check whether the rule applies to you.

likely_exempt.title: You're likely exempt.
likely_exempt.body: Based on what you told us, you likely don't need to meet the work rule.

meeting_requirement.title: The rule applies to you, and right now you're meeting it. Keep proof of every hour.
meeting_requirement.body: Save records for every hour of work, volunteering, or an approved program.

subject.title: The rule likely applies to you. At your next CalFresh renewal, you may need 80 hours a month of work, volunteering or an approved program.
subject.body: Start tracking now so you have proof ready. Ask your county when it starts for you.

ask_county.title: We can't tell from your answers. Your county can.
ask_county.body: Contact your county for help figuring out if the rule applies to you.

notes.title: Good to know
notes.job_search_outside_program: Job search on your own doesn't count. It only counts as part of a job program, like CalFresh E&T, WIOA or Trade Act.
notes.job_search_no_program: Job search counts only as part of a job program. None of these hours count this month.
notes.job_search_capped: Some of your job search hours aren't counted here. In a job program, job search counts only while it is less than your other program hours. Ask your program if yours is different.
notes.workfare_mixed: Workfare can't be added to your other hours, so the ring doesn't count it. Your county sets your workfare hours from your benefit amount. Ask them how many you need.
notes.workfare_only: The ring doesn't count workfare. Your county sets your workfare hours from your benefit amount. Ask them how many you need.

rule.title: How the rule works
rule.adds: If the rule applies to you, you need 80 hours a month. Work, volunteering and job programs add up.
rule.jobSearch: Job search counts only as part of a job program. Workfare is checked differently by your county.
rule.report: If the rule applies to you and your hours drop below 20 a week on average (80 a month), tell your county within 10 days.

about.title: About HourProof
about.what: HourProof helps people on CalFresh in California with the work rule: checking whether it likely applies, keeping track of hours, and keeping proof ready for the county.
about.notGov: HourProof is not CalFresh, your county or the State of California, and it is not connected to them. It can't see your case. Nothing here is a decision or legal advice. Only your county can decide whether the rule applies to you and whether your hours count.
about.rules: The questions and rules follow the state's instructions to counties (CDSS All County Letter 26-29) and Santa Clara County's handbook. Each screening question links to its source.
about.rulesLink: Read the state's letter (PDF, in English)
about.notReviewed: No caseworker or legal-aid worker has reviewed our reading of the rules yet. Until one does, HourProof never tells you that you are exempt. It says you may be, and to ask your county.
about.reviewed: Our reading of the rules was reviewed by {reviewer} on {date}.
about.who: HourProof is a student project, made for the 2026 Congressional App Challenge in California's 16th Congressional District. It is free and has no ads.
about.ai: Much of the code, and the first draft of the Spanish text, were written with AI tools. A log of what they did is kept with the code.
about.spanish: The Spanish text has not yet been checked by a native speaker. If something reads wrong, please tell us.
about.contactBenefits: For questions about your benefits or your case, call {county}:
about.contactApp: For questions about HourProof, or to ask us to remove your kitchen check-in records:

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.short: The short version: the hours you log and the documents you add stay on your phone. The only personal information HourProof receives is what you send when you check in at a kitchen.
privacy.onPhone1: Your answers to the screening questions. They are gone when you close the tab.
privacy.onPhone2: The hours you log, with any place or note you type.
privacy.onPhone3: The photos and PDF files you add as proof.
privacy.onPhone4: What you type into a CF 888 form. It is used to make the PDF on your phone and is not saved.
privacy.onPhone5: A copy of your hours, if you save one. It goes where you save it.
privacy.onPhoneNote: Because these stay only on your phone, nobody else can get them back for you. Clearing your browser's data, or losing the phone, removes them.
privacy.sent1: Your language choice (English or Spanish), as a cookie, so pages come back in the right language.
privacy.sent2: When you check in at a kitchen: the first name or nickname you type, the times you check in and out, which kitchen, and a random ID for your phone. There is no account, and we don't ask for an email address or a phone number.
privacy.sent3: Supervisors at that kitchen see your first name and your times, so they can confirm your hours. Their first name, and a reason if they don't accept a shift, are saved with the shift.
privacy.sent4: After you have checked in at a kitchen, your hour log asks HourProof for your kitchen shifts so it can show them.
privacy.never1: Your full name, birth date, address, case number or Social Security number.
privacy.never2: Your pay stubs or any other document.
privacy.neverNote: There are no ads and no tracking. We don't sell your information, and we don't give it to anyone except the kitchen you checked in at.
privacy.hostsTitle: The companies that run our computers
privacy.hosts: The pages come from Vercel. Kitchen check-in records are kept in a database run by Supabase, in the United States. Like any website, both receive your phone's internet address when it connects. We don't add it to your records.
privacy.keep1: On your phone: until you delete them or clear your browser's data.
privacy.keep2: Kitchen check-in records: until you ask us to remove them, or the project ends.
privacy.remove1: To delete hours, open the entry in your hour log, tap Edit, then Delete.
privacy.remove2: To remove everything HourProof saved on your phone, clear this site's data in your browser's settings.
privacy.remove3: To remove kitchen check-in records, contact us and tell us the kitchen, the date and the first name you used. We can't look you up any other way.
privacy.notGov: HourProof is a student project. It is not a government website.
privacy.sent5: If you link two browsers with a link code, HourProof saves that their two random IDs belong together, so each one can show the other's kitchen shifts.
